scenes.section: Start with something you already know

lines.raw: Simple definition.
lines.say: Simple definition.

lines.raw: Medicare is the US federal government's health insurance for people aged 65 and older, and for some younger people with long-term disabilities or serious kidney disease.
lines.say: Medicare is the U S federal government's health insurance for people aged 65 and older, and for some younger people with long-term disabilities or serious kidney disease.

lines.raw: It is run by **CMS**, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services.
lines.say: It is run by C M S, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services.

lines.raw: Who qualifies for Medicare?
lines.say: Who qualifies for Medicare?

lines.raw: The main ways people get Medicare (about 68 million people in 2025).
lines.say: The main ways people get Medicare (about 68 million people in 2025).

lines.raw: **Age 65 and older**. Rule: US citizens or long-term legal residents. This is the largest group. Example: Robert, from May 2022.
lines.say: Age 65 and older. Rule: U S citizens or long-term legal residents. This is the largest group. Example: Robert, from May 2022.

lines.raw: **Under 65 with a disability**. Rule: After receiving Social Security disability payments (**SSDI**) for **24 months**. Example: A 50-year-old builder who cannot work after a back injury.
lines.say: Under 65 with a disability. Rule: After receiving Social Security disability payments (S S D I) for 24 months. Example: A 50-year-old builder who cannot work after a back injury.

lines.raw: **Kidney failure (ESRD)**. Rule: People with **End-Stage Renal Disease** who need regular **dialysis** or a kidney transplant. Any age. Example: A 40-year-old on dialysis three times a week.
lines.say: Kidney failure (E S R D). Rule: People with End-Stage Renal Disease who need regular dialysis or a kidney transplant. Any age. Example: A 40-year-old on dialysis three times a week.

lines.raw: **ALS (Lou Gehrig's disease)**. Rule: A disease that slowly weakens the muscles. No 24-month wait: Medicare starts when disability payments start. Example: A 55-year-old diagnosed with ALS.
lines.say: A L S (Lou Gehrig's disease). Rule: A disease that slowly weakens the muscles. No 24-month wait: Medicare starts when disability payments start. Example: A 55-year-old diagnosed with A L S.

lines.raw: Who pays for Medicare?
lines.say: Who pays for Medicare?

lines.raw: Workers and employers each pay **1.45%** of wages as Medicare tax (2.9% in total).
lines.say: Workers and employers each pay 1.45 percent of wages as Medicare tax (2.9 percent in total).

lines.raw: This mainly funds **hospital** cover (Part A).
lines.say: This mainly funds hospital cover (Part A).

lines.raw: Doctor cover (Part B) is paid mostly from general government tax money, plus a monthly **premium** from each person on Medicare.
lines.say: Doctor cover (Part B) is paid mostly from general government tax money, plus a monthly premium from each person on Medicare.

lines.say: Insurers call their own customers "members"; Medicare calls them beneficiaries.

lines.raw: CMS.
lines.say: C M S.

lines.raw: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services: the federal agency that runs Medicare and oversees Medicaid.
lines.say: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services: the federal agency that runs Medicare and oversees Medicaid.

lines.raw: SSDI.
lines.say: S S D I.

lines.raw: Social Security Disability Insurance: monthly payments for people who worked but can no longer work because of a disability.
lines.say: Social Security Disability Insurance: monthly payments for people who worked but can no longer work because of a disability.

lines.raw: ESRD.
lines.say: E S R D.

lines.raw: End-Stage Renal Disease: permanent kidney failure that needs dialysis or a transplant.
lines.say: End-Stage Renal Disease: permanent kidney failure that needs dialysis or a transplant.

scenes.section: The Medicare card and the MBI

lines.raw: Every beneficiary gets a red, white and blue **Medicare card**.
lines.say: Every beneficiary gets a red, white and blue Medicare card.

lines.raw: The most important thing on it is the **Medicare Beneficiary Identifier (MBI)**: an 11-character ID used on every Medicare claim.
lines.say: The most important thing on it is the Medicare Beneficiary Identifier (M B I): an 11-character I D used on every Medicare claim.

lines.raw: Since 2018 to 2019, the MBI replaced the old ID that was based on the person's **Social Security number**, to reduce identity theft.
lines.say: Since 2018 to 2019, the M B I replaced the old I D that was based on the person's Social Security number, to reduce identity theft.

scenes.section: The Medicare card and the MBI

lines.raw: MBI tips for data work.
lines.say: M B I tips for data work.

lines.raw: The dashes are only printed on the card to make it easier to read.
lines.say: The dashes are only printed on the card to make it easier to read.

lines.raw: In data, the MBI is stored as **11 characters with no dashes**: `3TW7HC2AP58`.
lines.say: In data, the M B I is stored as 11 characters with no dashes: 3 T W 7 H C 2 A P 5 8.

lines.raw: It is random: it does **not** contain the birth date or any meaning.
lines.say: It is random: it does not contain the birth date or any meaning.

lines.raw: Letters that look like numbers (**S, L, O, I, B, Z**) are never used.
lines.say: Letters that look like numbers (S, L, O, I, B, Z) are never used.

lines.raw: When can people sign up?
lines.say: When can people sign up?

lines.raw: Medicare has fixed windows for joining and changing.
lines.say: Medicare has fixed windows for joining and changing.

lines.raw: Missing them can mean waiting, and sometimes paying a **late penalty** for life.
lines.say: Missing them can mean waiting, and sometimes paying a late penalty for life.

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: **Initial Enrollment Period (IEP)**. When: **7 months** around your 65th birthday: the 3 months before your birthday month, the birthday month, and the 3 months after. What you can do: Sign up for Medicare for the first time.
lines.say: Initial Enrollment Period (I E P). When: 7 months around your 65th birthday: the 3 months before your birthday month, the birthday month, and the 3 months after. What you can do: Sign up for Medicare for the first time.

lines.raw: **Annual Enrollment Period (AEP)**. When: **15 October to 7 December** every year. Changes start on **1 January**. What you can do: Switch between Original Medicare and Medicare Advantage, change plans, join or change a drug plan.
lines.say: Annual Enrollment Period (A E P). When: 15 October to 7 December every year. Changes start on 1 January. What you can do: Switch between Original Medicare and Medicare Advantage, change plans, join or change a drug plan.

lines.raw: **Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment**. When: **1 January to 31 March**. What you can do: People already in Medicare Advantage can switch to another one, or go back to Original Medicare, once.
lines.say: Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment. When: 1 January to 31 March. What you can do: People already in Medicare Advantage can switch to another one, or go back to Original Medicare, once.

lines.raw: **Special Enrollment Period (SEP)**. When: After certain life events. What you can do: Change plans after, for example, moving house or losing job-based insurance.
lines.say: Special Enrollment Period (S E P). When: After certain life events. What you can do: Change plans after, for example, moving house or losing job-based insurance.

lines.raw: Feb 2022: IEP opens.
lines.say: Feb 2022: I E P opens.

lines.raw: Robert turns 65 in May 2022, so his 7-month window runs from **February to August 2022**.
lines.say: Robert turns 65 in May 2022, so his 7-month window runs from February to August 2022.

lines.raw: Mar 2022: he signs up.
lines.say: Mar 2022: he signs up.

lines.say: He enrols through Social Security, choosing Parts A and B (Original Medicare).

lines.raw: 1 May 2022: coverage starts.
lines.say: 1 May 2022: coverage starts.

lines.raw: Because he signed up before his birthday month, Medicare starts on the **1st of his birthday month**.
lines.say: Because he signed up before his birthday month, Medicare starts on the 1st of his birthday month.

lines.raw: Nov 2023: AEP choice.
lines.say: Nov 2023: A E P choice.

lines.say: During the Annual Enrollment Period he picks a Medicare Advantage plan with drug cover.

lines.raw: 1 Jan 2024: new plan starts.
lines.say: 1 Jan 2024: new plan starts.

lines.raw: His Medicare Advantage plan begins.
lines.say: His Medicare Advantage plan begins.

lines.say: He keeps it for 2025.

lines.raw: Late penalties.
lines.say: Late penalties.

lines.raw: If someone does not sign up for Part B when they first can (and they have no job-based insurance), their Part B premium goes up by **10% for each full year** they waited, usually for as long as they have Medicare.
lines.say: If someone does not sign up for Part B when they first can (and they have no job-based insurance), their Part B premium goes up by 10 percent for each full year they waited, usually for as long as they have Medicare.

lines.raw: Part D (drugs) has its own late penalty too.
lines.say: Part D (drugs) has its own late penalty too.

lines.say: Why it matters for data.

lines.say: In data, these windows explain coverage start dates.

lines.raw: Most Medicare coverage starts on the **1st of a month**, and most plan changes start on **1 January**.
lines.say: Most Medicare coverage starts on the 1st of a month, and most plan changes start on 1 January.

lines.raw: Key takeaways.
lines.say: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: Medicare is US federal health insurance for people 65+, and some younger people with disabilities, ESRD or ALS.
lines.say: Medicare is U S federal health insurance for people 65+, and some younger people with disabilities, E S R D or A L S.

lines.raw: Under 65 with a disability: Medicare usually starts after 24 months of SSDI.
lines.say: Under 65 with a disability: Medicare usually starts after 24 months of S S D I.

lines.raw: ALS has no waiting period.
lines.say: A L S has no waiting period.

lines.raw: The MBI is an 11-character random ID, stored without dashes, used on every Medicare claim.
lines.say: The M B I is an 11-character random I D, stored without dashes, used on every Medicare claim.

lines.raw: The Initial Enrollment Period is 7 months around the 65th birthday.
lines.say: The Initial Enrollment Period is 7 months around the 65th birthday.

lines.raw: The Annual Enrollment Period is 15 October to 7 December.
lines.say: The Annual Enrollment Period is 15 October to 7 December.
